title: Space Data Link Security Protocol—Extended Procedures
organisation: Consultative Committee for Space Data Systems (CCSDS)
status_notes: Original issue according to the Document Control table (PDF p. 7).
summary:
The CCSDS Recommended Standard for the **auxiliary procedures needed to operate [SDLS](../ccsds/sdls.md) over a space link**. The SDLS Blue Book defines how frames are protected; this one defines how keys and Security Associations (SAs) are managed and how the on-board security function is monitored. The model is an Initiator, usually the mission operations centre, commanding a Recipient, usually the spacecraft.

Section 2 outlines three services:

* **Key Management**: a two-tier symmetric scheme of master keys and session keys, a key lifecycle from pre-activation through active and deactivated to destroyed, and Over-The-Air Rekeying (OTAR), which is recommended but optional for missions with pre-loaded keys.
* **SA Management**: a state model Null, Unkeyed, Keyed and Operational, with Create, Rekey, Start, Stop, Expire and Delete transitions, plus setting and reading the anti-replay sequence number (ARSN) and its window.
* **Monitoring and Control**: Ping, security log status, dump and erase, Self-Test and Alarm Flag Reset.

Section 3 defines each procedure. Section 4 covers interfaces. EP PDUs travel as packets on a dedicated TC MAP, a TM or AOS VC packet service or a USLP MAP, and they must be protected by SDLS authentication or authenticated encryption. Section 4 also defines the 32-bit **Frame Security Report (FSR)**, a new Type-2 OCF carried in TM, AOS or USLP frames and alternated with the CLCW. Section 5 gives the PDU formats: a TLV-based EP PDU with an 8-bit tag (command or reply, CCSDS or user, service group, procedure ID) and a 16-bit length. Sections 6 and 7 cover managed parameters and conformance. Annex D gives a baseline implementation: AES-GCM with 256-bit keys, 96-bit IV and 128-bit MAC for OTAR and key verification, at most 28 keys per OTAR command so that it fits a 1024-octet frame, and the reserved SPIs 0 and 65535 for EP traffic.

contents.title: Services Provided by SDLS Extended Procedures

key_points.text: The standard defines the Key Management, SA Management and SDLS Monitoring and Control services, their data structures and their interfaces with the SDL and SDLS protocols; it does not mandate cryptographic algorithms for key generation and management.
A goal is a new telemetry OCF type, the Frame Security Report, fully compatible with TM, AOS and USLP.
Initiator (usually the MOC) and Recipient (usually the spacecraft) are the two peers; the ARSN starts at zero when an SA is activated and increments for every frame sent on it.

Key management is a two-tier symmetric infrastructure: master keys (key-encryption keys) for management and session keys (traffic keys) for SDLS operations, refreshed by OTAR; OTAR is recommended but not required if a mission flies with pre-loaded keys only.

Key lifecycle states are Pre-Activation, Active, Deactivated and Destroyed, with Key Activation, Deactivation, Destruction and Verification transitions; the Suspended state of the Symmetric Key Management practice is not used.
SA state model: Null -(Create SA)-> Unkeyed -(Rekey SA)-> Keyed -(Start SA)-> Operational, reversed by Stop SA, Expire SA and Delete SA; static missions need only Start and Stop with pre-loaded SAs.
Because an OCF can hold only one control word, the FSR is multiplexed with the CLCW in a mission-specific pattern.
EP PDUs use a dedicated MAP of the TC MAP packet service, the TM or AOS VC packet service, or the USLP MAP packet service.

The 32-bit FSR holds Control Word Type '1' (1 bit; a CLCW is '0'), FSR Version Number '100' (3 bits), Alarm flag (1), Bad SN, Bad MAC and Bad SA flags (1 bit each), Last SPI (16) and the 8 LSBs of the ARSN (8), and it is sampled for each received SDLS-protected frame.
The FSR Alarm Flag latches at '1' once any frame has been rejected by the Recipient Security Function and stays set until reset by a dedicated command; the other flags reflect only the last frame.

All EP command PDUs must be sent over an SDLS channel protected by authentication or authenticated encryption; the reserved SPIs 0 and 65535 may be used for EP traffic, and using a different SA from the one being affected is good practice.
EP commands and replies use a TLV format: an 8-bit Tag (Procedure Type, User Flag, 2-bit Service Group, 4-bit Procedure ID) and a 16-bit Data Field Length in bits.

Service Group values: 00 Key Management, 01 SA Management for Initiator-to-Recipient SAs, 10 SA Management for Recipient-to-Initiator SAs, 11 Security Monitoring and Control; Table 5-1 assigns procedure IDs (for example OTAR 0001, Start SA 1011, Ping 0001).

SA management managed parameters include SPI 1-65534, service type, Security Header IV (1-32 octets), SN (2-8 octets), PL (1-2 octets) and Trailer MAC (8-64 octets) lengths, the authentication bit mask, ARSN and ARSN window.
Baseline mode: FSR as OCF Type 2 alternating with the CLCW when COP-1 reports on the same VC, no TLV nesting, and the two reserved SPIs for EP PDUs.
Baseline OTAR and Key Verification use AES-GCM with 256-bit keys, a 96-bit IV and a 128-bit MAC; Key Destruction and Key Inventory are not in the baseline.

A baseline OTAR command carries a 16-bit master key ID, a 96-bit IV, N encrypted key blocks of 272 bits (16-bit key ID plus 256-bit key) and a 128-bit MAC, with N <= 28 so that the PDU (at most 995 octets) fits a 1024-octet frame.

notes: Companion to the library item ccsds-355-0-355x0b2 (SDLS issue 2), although its normative reference [1] is SDLS issue 1 (355.0-B-1, 2015); the concept Green Book is ccsds-350-5-350x5g2 (issue 2; [C3] cites issue 1), and the algorithms [7] are ccsds-352-0-352x0b2. Cited as reference [22] by ccsds-350-5-350x5g2 and mentioned in A1 of ccsds-350-0-350x0g3. Other normative references are 2015-era issues (TM SDLP B-2, AOS B-3, TC SDLP B-3, USLP B-1, SPP B-1), older than the library items. Inconsistencies as printed: the note to 2.3.2 says only the Suspended key state is unused and Compromised applies to the Initiator, while the note to 5.4.1.2 says both Suspended and Compromised are not used; [C13] is titled 'Summary of Concept of Rationale' (sic) and is 'Forthcoming'; [2] is still a draft Red Book. The managed SPI range is 1-65534, while 4.3.1.2 allows the reserved SPIs 0 and 65535 for EP PDUs. PDF pages 1 and 2 are duplicate covers; the extraction has 130 PDF pages (registry: 129). No individual authors are named.
